marks.gloss_en: ואידך, אי מהתם איכא למימר חזה ושוק של תודה -- from that verse one could say the comparison is to the breast and thigh of a thanks-offering (Steinsaltz: eaten one day and a night)
ואידך, אמר קרא 'לך יהיה' -- הוסיף לך הכתוב הויה אחרת בבכור (= p_lecha_yihyeh_havaya)
Rav: 'it shall be yours' -- Scripture added another 'being' for the firstborn
the school of Rav: this 'it shall be yours' teaches that a blemished firstborn is given to the priest, which we find nowhere else in the whole Torah
Rav: 'and their flesh' -- both unblemished and blemished
תניא נמי הכי -- in the baraita both tannaim forbid with corneal blemishes
תניא נמי הכי -- the baraita's R' Yehuda permits only with body blemishes, so that is where the tannaim divide
תניא נמי הכי -- R' Meir forbids body blemishes 'because of those that change': a decree on account of the corneal case
the baraita, R' Yehuda: with corneal blemishes it is forbidden, because they change
one who slaughters the firstborn and then shows its blemish: R' Yehuda permits
with blemishes on the cornea, all agree [the slaughtered firstborn] is forbidden
תא שמע, דתניא: ... אבל מפני השבת אבידה לבעלים אמרו רשאי לקיימו שלשים יום -- thirty days are granted beyond the year
a firstborn nowadays, until it has [a blemish] fit to show a sage, may be kept two or three years
ועדיין תיבעי לי: שלשים יום אחר שנתו, או דלמא קודם שנתו? -- the baraita's thirty days may be for a blemish arising after the year, so the question stands
תא שמע: נולד לו מום בחמשה עשר יום בתוך שנתו משלימין לו חמשה עשר יום אחר שנתו. שמע מינה
מסייע לרבי אלעזר -- fifteen plus fifteen is thirty days from the blemish
a blemish arose fifteen days [before the end of] its year -- one completes for it fifteen days after its year
reading (a): a blemish within its year -- twelve months, and after its year thirty more as well
after its year he may not keep it even one day, even one hour
R' Elazar (version 2): a firstborn blemished within its year is given thirty days after its year
